text:
maria: Quick update from the tail-latency run this morning — ran the mixed-kernel routing + tighter wait window experiment across 4x A100 nodes.
ashwin: nice, what knobs did you change exactly?
maria: Two main changes:
  - scheduler.max_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 2048
  - scheduler.max_wait_ms: 16 -> 6
  - enabled kernel_fallback for long sequences (fp16->int8 fallback path)
kai: also did we change prefix/KV cache TTL or anything that could affect cold-hit p99?
maria: KV config unchanged, cache hit-rate stayed ~93% on the run — most tails are dispatch/queue delays not cache misses.
olivia: curious numbers — p95/p99 shift?
maria: p50 ~= unchanged (1.9ms per token on avg). p95 down ~12%. p99 improved ~18% but p99.9 still spikes occasionally.
ashwin: can you paste the perf summary?
maria: pasted short summary:
```
workload: 1k rps mixed-short+long
old (4096/16): p50=1.9ms p95=9.8ms p99=38ms p99.9=110ms
new (2048/6) : p50=2.0ms p95=8.6ms p99=31ms p99.9=98ms
kv-hit-rate: 93% -> 92.7% (no meaningful change)
cpu sched wait avg: 3.7ms -> 2.1ms
queue-length tail: 95th pct drops by 22%
``` 
kai: interesting that p50 nudged up slightly; likely fewer coalesced batches so less batching efficiency for short requests.
olivia: Did you capture kernel selection traces? want to see how often fallback hit
maria: yes, trace snippet:
```
[route] kernel=A10-fused (short) -> 78%
[route] kernel=BatchedAttention (medium) -> 14%
[route] kernel=int8-fallback (long) -> 8%
```
maria: fallback rate slightly higher on long tails vs baseline but latency for those is better due to reduced queue time.
ashwin: Any effect on GPU utilization / tokens/sec?
maria: tokens/sec fell ~6% at peak, GPU util more uniform (less sawtooth), and overall token cost per 1M tokens improved by ~3% (fewer retry/fallback lat spikes -> fewer retries upstream)
kai: what about max_batch_tokens tradeoff? 2048 seems to reduce tail but hurts throughput slightly — did you try 3072 as a middle ground?
maria: yes ran a quick sweep: 4096/16, 3072/10, 2048/6. 3072/10 had p99 ~34ms and throughput ~-2% — profile shows best cost/latency Pareto often around 3072/10 for mixed workloads.
olivia: profile flamegraph for scheduler hot path?
maria: attached flame snippet (copied small excerpt):
```
scheduler::enqueue 32%
scheduler::select_kernel 20%
kernel_dispatch 18%
batching::coalesce 12%
kv::lookup 8%
others 10%
```
maria: select_kernel cost is non-trivial — optimizable by caching heuristic mapping for common prompt shapes.
ashwin: did you try warming the kernel selector map or a LRU for kernel decisions?
maria: I prototype cached decision key = (seq_len_bucket, kv_hit, model_variant). warm-cache reduced select_kernel CPU by ~60% in microbench.
kai: what about tail noise sources — long GC in user code, or scheduler starving bursts?
maria: we correlated requests with routing tags; tails correlate with occasional 1-2% traffic bursts with long sequences from conversational sessions. Those get starved under large batch windows.
olivia: any changes to fallback thresholds? maybe prefer faster kernel for tail even if slightly worse FLOPs.
maria: swapped fallback threshold to favor lower latency (prefer fused kernels for <1.5k tokens) — reduced p99 by 6% but increased avg token cost for long jobs by ~1.4%.
ashwin: do we think this is a good default for Hosted vs Dedicated? Hosted wants predictable p99, Dedicated customers often prefer throughput.
maria: proposal: default scheduling profile = "latency-sensitive" (max_batch_tokens=3072, max_wait_ms=8, kernel_priority=latency), Dedicated can use "throughput" profile (4096/20, kernel_priority=efficiency).
kai: can we make profiles per-route so customers can select on a per-deployment basis?
maria: yes Console change is straightforward — slider for latency vs cost, maps to these config presets. I'll open a PR for api + console mapping.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for runtime-configs/latency-presets @maria
olivia: next steps: run 24h soak on latency-sensitive preset, collect p99.9 and error rates; if no regressions, ship as default for hosted.
maria: I'll queue soak and post a summary tomorrow. any other quick asks?
ashwin: include kernel decision cache metrics and a histogram of queue wait times per route pls.
maria: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
